text:
Mike: Seeing NVMe latency spikes in eu-west3 during bulk checkpointing; GPU attaches are failing with PREEMPT, seems iowait-related. Anyone else?
Anya: yup, alerts came in ~5m ago. attach failures up ~3% in the cluster. traces point to a tiny-writes pattern from checkpoint-writer + janitor overlap causing IO queue clog.
Storage Bot: ALERT: nvme_iops(scratchpool-euw3) > 120000 for 5m. avg_lat_ms=4.2, p99_lat_ms=120. recent events: attach_failures++.
Lucas: Quick mitigation idea: throttle janitor + enable coalescing for checkpoint writes. Can we try an adaptive janitor throttle on a small canary (rate_limit_ops=1000) and see?
Mike: Need exact steps. Also want fallout matrix — if we throttle janitor we delay cleanup and increase disk pressure over days. Cost tradeoffs noted.
Natalie: Draft patch: janitor helm values update -> `janitor.rate_limit_ops: 1000`, `janitor.burst: 2000`, `janitor.sustain: 800`. Canary on 10 nodes first.
Anya: Also kernel tweaks that help: set `vm.dirty_ratio=5`, `vm.dirty_background_ratio=1` on canary hosts to reduce small sync bursts from checkpoints.
Lucas: Short-term trick: mount a tmpfs aggregator for /var/checkpoints on canary nodes, flush with `rsync --bwlimit` and `ionice` to disk async. Coalesces tinywrites into bigger batches.
Mike: Rollout plan:
  1) Apply janitor throttle to gnode-euw3-41..50 (10 nodes)
  2) Enable tmpfs aggregator on same nodes
  3) Apply kernel tunables via kexec config on those hosts
  4) Monitor metrics: nvme_iops, nvme_qdepth, attach_success_rate, nvme_p99
  5) If stable for 24h, promote to region
Who's oncall to run this?
sre-oncall: I'm oncall. I can run the canary now and watch alerts. SLOs to validate: attach_success >= 99.5%, attach_fail_rate < 0.5%, nvme_p99 < 40ms.
Storage Bot: RUNBOOK: if attach_fail_rate > 5% after canary rollback to prior janitor config and escalate to infra owners.
Anya: For traces, capture blktrace/blkparse on canary nodes:
```
sudo blktrace -d /dev/nvme0n1 -o - | blkparse -i - -v
```
That will show queueing pattern and tiny write coalescing.
Mike: :thumbsup: Oncall, start canary and post a short status update in 10m. If this clears, we'll document a longer-term design (write-aggregator service + smarter janitor scheduling).
sre-oncall: Starting canary now on gnode-euw3-41..50. Applying janitor flags and tmpfs aggregator mount. Will report back in 10m.
Storage Bot: ACTION: throttle applied to gnode-euw3-41..50. nvme_iops dropped 110k -> 35k within 90s. p99 latency dropped 120ms -> 28ms. attach_success improved from 96.8% -> 99.7% in canary set.
Lucas: Great signal. Next: bake tmpfs aggregator into helm chart and run 72h watch. Need perf testing for longer checkpoint windows.
Natalie: PR opened with helm diff + metrics: link: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/helm/compare/1234 (will add reviewers). Tracked metrics: nvme_iops, nvme_qdepth, attach_fail_rate, janitor_ops.
Anya: Cost note: tmpfs aggregator then rsync increases CPU + ephemeral network usage; estimate ~+$120/day for full region rollout. Adding to ticket and CCing finance for rough approval.
sre-oncall: Can confirm +30m steady. Will keep logging and will send hourly updates. If anything flares, I'll rollback janitor flags immediately.
Mike: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this thread as the rollout record and spin up a follow-up RFC for the long-term write-aggregation strategy.
